newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ATLAS COPCO SAYS PRIME BUY MEANS SERVICE SYNERGIES.
newsitem.headline: ATLAS COPCO SAYS PRIME BUY MEANS SERVICE SYNERGIES.

text.p: Atlas Copco said on Wednesday it expected its acquisition of U.S. rental equipment company Prime Services to mean synergies on the service side.
The company said it expected a turnaround for a somewhat stronger European construction market in the second half of 1997 and in 1998.

"Prime should be seen as a service company. Of 2,200 employees, 750 are mechanics and 300 truck drivers who deliver goods to customers," Atlas Copco chief executive Giulio Mazzalupi told a news conference.
"This organisation can be used for service and in connection with sales of our production," he said.
Mazzalupi did not, however, see rental operations as a strategic move for Atlas, particularly not in Europe.
"I'm a bit hesitant about rental operations in Europe. I believe more in the accessories side. I would love to have proper rental operations in Asia but the market is not ripe for it yet," he said.
Mazzalupi said the European construction market was stable.
"We think, however, that it will improve somewhat in the second half of 1997 and in 1998. Previously we believed in a continued fall," he said.
But he warned that Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) and the convergence criteria linked to it put certain question marks on how fast the market will turn.
